The deletion reorganizes local 3D chromatin architecture in the region.
NF1 haploinsufficiency plus a somatic second hit in the Schwann-cell lineage drives neurofibroma formation via RAS-MAPK hyperactivation.
SUZ12/PRC2 haploinsufficiency lowers the dosage reserve and predisposes to malignant transformation of plexiform neurofibromas into MPNST.

meta.association: Co-deleted gene contributing to neurodevelopmental phenotype

nodes.description: Co-deletion of CRLF3 contributes to the neurodevelopmental phenotype independently of NF1-driven neural stem cell proliferation effects. Patient-derived iPSC cerebral organoid modeling links reduced CRLF3 expression and impaired RhoA signaling to defective neuronal maturation.

evidence.reference_title: Patient-derived iPSC-cerebral organoid modeling of the 17q11.2 microdeletion syndrome establishes CRLF3 as a critical regulator of neurogenesis.
evidence.snippet: maturation defects are caused by reduced cytokine receptor-like factor 3 (CRLF3) expression and impaired RhoA signaling.

nodes.description: Microdeletion patients characteristically develop cutaneous neurofibromas at an earlier age and in larger numbers than typical NF1 patients, and plexiform neurofibromas are common; a subset carry an extreme internal tumor burden.

evidence.reference_title: Expanding the phenotype of neurofibromatosis type 1 microdeletion syndrome.
evidence.snippet: We note 38/56 (67.9%) with describable facial features, 25/57 (43.8%) with plexiform neurofibromas, and 3/57 (5.2%) with malignant peripheral nerve sheath tumors within the observed period.

nodes.description: Global developmental delay, cognitive impairment, and learning difficulties are more frequent and more severe in microdeletion patients than in classic NF1.

evidence.reference_title: Emerging genotype-phenotype relationships in patients with large NF1 deletions.
evidence.snippet: Patients with germline type-1 NF1 microdeletions frequently exhibit dysmorphic facial features, overgrowth/tall-for-age stature, significant delay in cognitive development, large hands and feet, hyperflexibility of joints and muscular hypotonia.

nodes.description: Lifetime risk of MPNST is substantially higher in microdeletion patients (approximately 16-26%) than in NF1 patients with intragenic mutations (8-13%), contributing to reduced life expectancy.

evidence.reference_title: Emerging genotype-phenotype relationships in patients with large NF1 deletions.
evidence.snippet: their lifetime MPNST risk is 16-26%, rather higher than that of NF1 patients with intragenic NF1 mutations (8-13%).

nodes.description: The recurrent ~1.4 Mb type-1 deletion is generated by non-allelic homologous recombination between the flanking NF1-REP low-copy repeats, removing the NF1 gene together with 14 protein-coding genes and four microRNA genes. Complete loss of one NF1 allele produces neurofibromin haploinsufficiency and consequent dysregulation of RAS-MAPK signaling, while co-deletion of dosage-sensitive neighbors accounts for the additional, non-NF1 features.

evidence.reference_title: Emerging genotype-phenotype relationships in patients with large NF1 deletions.
evidence.snippet: The majority of these deletions encompass 1.4-Mb and are associated with the loss of 14 protein-coding genes and four microRNA genes.

evidence.reference_title: Correlation between large rearrangements and patient phenotypes in NF1 deletion syndrome: an update and review.
evidence.snippet: The most frequent NF1 large deletion is 1.4 Mb, resulting from homologous recombination between two low copy repeats.

meta.association: Co-deleted PRC2 subunit increasing MPNST risk

nodes.description: The type-1 deletion also removes SUZ12, a core subunit of Polycomb Repressive Complex 2 (PRC2). Constitutional hemizygosity for SUZ12, followed by further PRC2 disruption at the tumor level, is implicated in the elevated risk of malignant peripheral nerve sheath tumor observed in microdeletion patients relative to those with intragenic NF1 mutations.

evidence.reference_title: Emerging genotype-phenotype relationships in patients with large NF1 deletions.
evidence.snippet: Co-deletion of the SUZ12 gene in addition to NF1 further increases the MPNST risk in NF1 microdeletion patients.

nodes.description: The MEK1/2 inhibitor selumetinib is used for symptomatic, inoperable plexiform neurofibromas in NF1 and is applicable to microdeletion patients with plexiform tumors; it is not specific to the microdeletion itself.

evidence.snippet: MEK inhibitors selumetinib or mirdametinib can reduce the size and symptoms associated with inoperable plexiform neurofibromas in many individuals with NF1.

nodes.description: Beyond simple gene-dosage loss, the 1.4 Mb deletion reorganizes local 3D chromatin architecture in the 17q11.2 region, producing position effects on the expression of genes flanking the deletion breakpoints.

evidence.reference_title: Genetic/epigenetic effects in NF1 microdeletion syndrome: beyond the haploinsufficiency, looking at the contribution of not deleted genes.
evidence.snippet: the 1.4-Mb deletion leads to changes in the 3D chromatin structure in the 17q11.2 region.
